questions: QuoteAPI|on_screening_outage (gap:declared:OD-1): What must QuoteAPI do when ScreeningService.screen fails with ScreeningUnavailableError (e.g. response status, storage/notification behaviour, retry or hold semantics)?

response|hold_presence (UNKNOWN): For non-priced held states like review_hold and refused_screening, which response fields must be present or absent (e.g. must price be omitted/null, must quote_id always be present, any additional hold-related fields)?

claims.text: Request validation rules for shipper_id, weight_kg, distance_km, declared_value, and behaviour on invalid requests are fully specified and verified.
Weight, distance, and declared value numeric bounds are as stated and govern validity.
On storage failure, nothing else runs (no screening, pricing, or notification) and status must be error: store_unavailable.
Screening decision table DT-S (accept/review/refuse) and associated statuses, notification behaviour, and pricing flags are normative for successful screening outcomes.
Pricing decision table DT-P (P1–P4) defines the price computation formula, surcharges, ordering, and rounding.
The overall flow order is validate > store > screen > decide > price > notify > respond.
Response field presence for quote_id and price is governed by: quote_id whenever a draft was stored; price only on priced rows of DT-S.
Notification failures are fire-and-forget and never alter the stored quote or the response.
